newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-SPRINGBOKS LOSE HURTER FOR WALLABY TEST.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SPRINGBOKS LOSE HURTER FOR WALLABY TEST.

text.p: South Africa selectors on Tuesday made one change for this weekend's Tri-Nations rugby union test against Australia by naming prop Dawie Theron to replace a flu-ridden Marius Hurter.
Theron was named in the starting line-up after a brief appearance as a reserve during the Springboks' 35-32 defeat by New Zealand in the series opener in Johannesburg on July 19.
Hooker James Dalton recovered from the calf strain that forced him to miss the All Black test but failed to oust Naka Drotske and had to settle for a place on the reserves bench.
Centre Japie Mulder failed a fitness test on a shoulder injury and will now pin his hopes on the return match against New Zealand in Auckland on August 9.
"Marius was left out after being unable to train at all on Monday because of the 'flu," a team spokesman told Reuters by telephone from Brisbane, where the test will be played.
Both Australia and South Africa must win on Saturday to revive their campaign after losing their opening matches against New Zealand.

Australia's crushing 33-18 defeat by the All Blacks on Saturday provoked an angry outburst by former Wallaby test flanker Simon Poidevin, who labelled coach Greg Smith's tactics as outdated and confused.
"It's very frustrating watching the team playing like a club side," Poidevin, his country's most capped forward with 59 tests, told The Australian newspaper on Tuesday.
"The Australian team's on-field performance seems confused and at times directionless. Ultimately the responsibility for the style and tactics must lie with coach Greg Smith," he said.
Australia are set to make at least three changes to the side beaten by New Zealand after dropping number eight Michael Brial and losing fly-half Tim Horan and fullback Matt Burke to injury.
Fullback Stephen Larkham is almost certain to replace Burke, while Troy Coker is the most likely candidate to fill the back row position.
Veteran fly-half David Knox was also recalled in a move that prompted a scathing response from local media given Smith's past refusal to consider him as a test candidate.
"If Smith was a gymnast, his backflip was worthy of an Olympic gold," The Australian said of Smith's change of heart in selecting Knox.

After naming a 23-man squad on Monday, Smith labelled Knox an "automatic choice". Yet two days earlier, Smith said Knox was a "non-tackler" who represented too great a risk because of his defensive frailties.
Reserve back rower Owen Finegan was also called up as cover for lock Garrick Morgan, who suffered mild concussion on Saturday and remains in doubt for the Springbok clash.

South Africa - 15-Russell Bennett, 14-Andre Snyman, 13-Percy Montgomery, 12-Danie van Schalkwyk, 11-Pieter Rossouw, 10-Jannie de Beer, 9-Joost van der Westhuizen, 8-Gary Teichmann (captain), 7-Andre Venter, 6-Ruben Kruger, 5-Mark Andrews, 4-Krynauw Otto, 3-Dawie Theron, 2-Naka Drotske, 1-Os du Randt.

Australia (from) - Stephen Larkham, Joe Roff, James Holbeck, Jason Little, Ben Tune, David Knox, George Gregan; Troy Coker, Owen Finegan, Brett Robinson, Daniel Manu, David Wilson, Matt Cockbain, John Eales (captain), Garrick Morgan, Richard Harry, Michael Foley, Marco Caputo, Andrew Heath, Andrew Blades.
